candidates.title: Gordie Howe bridge surpasses 1M vehicle crossings while other bridges, tunnel lose traffic
candidates.description: The Gordie Howe International Bridge has seen more than a million crossings since it officially opened to vehicle traffic on July 27, according to new numbers from the Bridge and Tunnel Operators Association.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Alberta has tabled a bill for new riding maps. What could a court challenge mean?
candidates.description: Alberta’s controversial new riding map is one step closer to implementation after Justice Minister Mickey Amery tabled a bill in the legislature on Monday. But legal experts say a potential court challenge could introduce a high level of uncertainty in advance of the next provincial election.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Father calls for apology after son target of racist taunts at Kitchener, Ont., hockey tournament
candidates.description: The father of a 16-year-old hockey player says he wants a public apology and cultural-competency training for the league after his son was the target of racist taunts at a tournament in Kitchener, Ont., on Nov. 8.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: N.L. premier waiting to hear from Quebec on Churchill River power deal
candidates.description: Quebec Energy Minister Stéphane Paquet said the Churchill River power deal is not set in stone, setting off a series of questions for Premier Tony Wakeham in Newfoundland and Labrador's House of Assembly.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Toronto police arrest suspect in Bridle Path home invasion investigation
candidates.description: Toronto police say one man has been arrested in connection with a violent home invasion last month in the city's Bridle Path neighbourhood.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Montreal students reeling from police violence at Nov. 13 education austerity protest
candidates.description: Montreal students are denouncing the Service de police de la Ville de Montréal (SPVM) for what they call unjustified acts of violence during a protest against education austerity that took place on Friday.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: 1 man, 2 children dead in Burlington, Ont., house fire, Ontario Fire Marshal says
candidates.description: A man, a 12-year-old child and a one-year-old boy are dead following a house fire in Burlington, Ont., the Ontario Fire Marshal said Monday morning in a news briefing.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Canada presented itself as a global leader in methane reductions at COP31. But is Alberta holding it back?
candidates.description: Canada took centre stage at COP31 last week to showcase its track record on cutting methane emissions. But some experts say the country can't be a global leader on reducing methane until Alberta, Canada's largest oil and gas producer, updates its equivalent regulations.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: North Atlantic right whales no match for vessel strikes, entanglements between Canada and U.S.
candidates.description: With the latest estimates putting the North Atlantic right whale population at just 382, a consortium is calling for urgent action to safeguard the species' survival.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: How an Ottawa man played 365 rec sports games in less than a year
candidates.description: On Jan. 1, Kenny MacDonald set a goal to play 365 recreational sport games in Ottawa before the year came to a close. On Sunday, he completed his mission at the Bell Sensplex in Kanata. The CBC's Emma Weller was there.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Quebecor makes $31B offer to acquire Telus
candidates.description: Proposed deal would combine complementary networks, spectrum and operating capabilities. But the deal would require approval from authorities including the Competition Bureau, and the federal government has been trying to boost competition among telecom companies.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: WestJet denied family's cancelled flight was actually cancelled, claiming passenger rights didn't apply
candidates.description: A family thought they'd have to cancel a long-awaited trip to Hawaii after WestJet scrapped their return flight. The airline initially refused to rebook them on a same-day flight with another carrier, dismissing the cancellation as a "schedule change."
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: N.L. families to receive $500 per child before the end of the year
candidates.description: Families in Newfoundland and Labrador who receive the Canada Child Benefit will receive $500 per child under the age of 18 as part of the province’s latest affordability measure connected to skyrocketing oil revenues.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Coroner's inquest into Alberta woman's death in Kenora, Ont., slated to start today
candidates.description: A coroner’s inquest into the death of a 29-year-old Alberta woman at Lake of the Woods District Hospital (LWDH) in Kenora, Ont., is expected to start later Monday morning. Here is what we know about the upcoming proceedings.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: 3 friends complete 8,000-km canoe journey across Canada, arriving at Vancouver's Jericho Beach
candidates.description: After more than 200 days, thousands of kilometres and countless hours on the water, three longtime friends from Toronto completed their canoe journey from Quebec to B.C. on Sunday at Vancouver's Jericho Beach.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Do Quebec police recruits get enough racial profiling training? We checked the curriculum
candidates.description: At Quebec's police academy, aspiring officers spend hundreds of hours on technical skills, from firing weapons to physically restraining suspects. Far less of their time explicitly addresses issues such as racial profiling and ethical breaches — which led to the firing of seven Montreal police officers earlier this month.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: CBSA demoting border officers who permanently lost ability to use sidearm
candidates.description: The Canada Border Services Agency has informed 63 employees that they will have to take on new, lower-paid positions because of medical conditions that prevent them from carrying a sidearm.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Journalists call for justice after reporter found dead in Mexican coastal city of Acapulco
candidates.description: A Mexican journalist was found dead on Saturday on the outskirts of Acapulco, a popular resort city in the southern Guerrero state, marking the latest in a string of alleged attacks targeting reporters in the country.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: United Airlines says issue affecting departing flights has been resolved
candidates.description: United Airlines said Monday that it had resolved a technology issue that delayed departing flights, just days after a malfunction in the U.S. Federal Aviation Administration's network prompted a nationwide ground stop.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: The U.K. is granting pardons to women convicted for having abortions

candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: U.S. Supreme Court set to hear 3 major Trump agenda immigration cases
candidates.description: The U.S. Supreme Court made at least two significant rulings to shape immigration policy last year. In the coming months, there will at least three more opinions that could be impactful, as U.S. President Donald Trump's administration seeks to reinterpret a number of laws concerning asylum, deportations and the detention of unauthorized persons in the U.S.

candidates.title: The battle for Trump's 'Trash Island' golf course | About That

candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Silicon Valley leaders call for reinstatement of Nvidia CEO with 'Stand With Jensen' petition
